newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher on strong results.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher on strong results.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Thursday as investors were encouraged by a rash of good corporate results, but shares in the oil giants whose profit gains had brightened the mood were hit by profit-taking.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.70 points, or 0.39 percent, at 1,992.47 at 0900 GMT while the CAC-40 September futures contract was five points higher at 1,997.
Traders said the market is waiting for Prime Minister Alain Juppe's tax reform address scheduled for Thursday evening.
Shares in food group Danone and retailer Carrefour rose after reporting first-half profit gains.
But oil groups Elf-Aquitaine and Total, which showed big earnings gains, fell on profit-taking after a recent rise.
